llm.summary: The skill is a clearly documented self-hosted speech service, but users must treat configured servers, staged files, and voice-cloning inputs as sensitive.

dimensions.detail: Network access, local shell commands, large model downloads, and persistent data directories are proportionate to a local speech server but carry privacy and resource impact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses Docker images, host data volumes, port publishing, curl, and optional GPU access; these are normal for this self-hosted service and are documented, though users should avoid exposing an unauthenticated server.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions repeatedly warn that text, audio, URLs, and voice samples are sent to the configured TALKIES_URL, and they constrain agents to only read/delete files they staged in the current user-approved workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side staged files, URL-download cache, models, and custom voices persist under the Talkies data directory; the artifact prominently discloses this and recommends auth, cleanup, and consent for voice cloning.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: ASR, TTS, URL transcription, file staging, MCP tools, and voice cloning all match the stated talkies speech-service purpose and are disclosed in the skill metadata and docs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only for a Talkies server you run or explicitly trust. Use localhost or HTTPS, enable TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN for shared or exposed deployments, do not send confidential text/audio or private URLs to untrusted servers, clean up staged files, and only use voice-cloning samples with the speaker's informed consent.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The TTS examples send input text to the configured Talkies endpoint, which is core functionality and is explicitly warned about as data leaving the host.
[E1] expected: The cloned-voice example uses a server-side custom voice and transmits synthesis input; this is purpose-aligned and paired with consent and trusted-server warnings.
[E1] expected: The later TTS workflow repeats the same external transmission pattern and is adequately disclosed rather than hidden.
